messages:
alex.sr_support: Hey team — customer reports repeated 429s over a ~3min burst. They sent a few request IDs but no HAR. Need a concise checklist we can send and a repro plan. Affected account: acme-inc (internal ticket 5421).

maya.sre: Thanks. Can you paste the request IDs and any response headers they captured? Also need the approximate UTC timeframe and the client IPs if available.

alex.sr_support: Pasted from the customer (redacted):

"2026-03-16T22:14:03Z req=01H8QZC2X0FJ1A0K9G3H4J5 Response: 429 Too Many Requests
  X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
  X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
  X-RateLimit-Reset: 164
"

"2026-03-16T22:14:34Z req=01H8QZD9L2AB2C1D0E6F7G Response: 429
"

"2026-03-16T22:15:01Z req=01H8QZFA7M3BC2D1E9H0J Response: 200
"

alex.sr_support: They say this pattern repeats every hour for a 2–3 minute window. No HAR, they are on a corporate NAT (no stable client IP shown).

maya.sre: Ok. Send them this minimal evidence checklist (copy/paste):
1) Capture a HAR from Chrome (Network tab -> right click -> Save as HAR). Include the full request/response headers for the failing calls.
2) For a quick repro: run curl with -v and include the request-id header we ask for, e.g.:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: 01H8QZC2X0FJ1A0K9G3H4J5" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"test"}' \
  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate
```

Ask them to attach the full verbose output (stdout+stderr) and to include the HTTP response headers (curl -D -).
3) Export any proxy/load-balancer logs around the UTC window (±5 minutes) — we need client IPs and connection counts per second.
4) If possible, run a replay at controlled rates so we can reproduce the burst: see script below.
5) Run our diagnostic helper (if they've installed it) to collect a debug bundle and provide the bundle ID. If not installed, we'll accept a tarball of logs.

jamie_platform: Adding repro script + timing capture they can run locally (low-risk):

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
REQ_ID_BASE=01H8QZC2
TOKEN="Bearer <REDACTED>"
for i in {1..60}; do
  RID="${REQ_ID_BASE}$(printf "%04d" $i)"
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total} %{size_download}\n" \
    -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" \
    -H "X-Request-ID: $RID" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"input":"ping"}' \
    https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate
  sleep 0.5   # 2 rps -> adjust to reproduce the burst shape
done
```

jamie_platform: That prints HTTP status, total request time and response size per call. Ask them to run this once within the affected window and paste output. That helps us correlate request timestamps with our logs.

maya.sre: Also request they include raw response headers for any 429s (we need X-RateLimit-* and X-Request-ID). If they only have a single request-id per call, tell them to set X-Request-ID on their client so we can match it.

alex.sr_support: I'll send the checklist and script now.

ops-bot: [ticket created] Ticket #5421 assigned to support (sla: 48h). Debug-bundle template: run `redwood-diagnostics collect --outfile debug-5421.tar.gz` and upload to the ticket.

maya.sre: One more internal note for triage: if we see matching request IDs on our side, check for sudden connection bursts (many simultaneous TCP new connections) or token reuse from many client IPs which can trip rate windows. Also check for proxy retries — clients that retry on 5xx can create micro-bursts.

jamie_platform: If they can't produce HAR, the minimal artifact we need to unblock triage: (a) three consecutive request IDs that returned 429 + response headers, (b) curl -v output for one failing and one succeeding call, (c) debug bundle or LB logs.

alex.sr_support: Great — I'll collect responses and post back here. :thumbsup:
